title: PGx draft curation proposal (unreviewed legacy migration candidate)
description: One conclusion this project reached about the science before WP-08, recovered from its legacy files so it is not lost, and written down as a candidate for review (WP-08). A proposal is NOT evidence, NOT a curation, NOT scientifically reviewed and NOT executable. It lives outside the evidence store on purpose. Nothing in this document may be used to assess a person. Its status and warnings are fixed by the schema, so a file that merely edited them into something friendlier does not validate.

proposal_id.description: Stable across runs over the same legacy files, so two extractions can be compared.

subject.description: What the legacy row was about, in the legacy file's own terms.

status.description: The only status this document may carry. There is no APPROVED, no ACCEPTED and no PENDING: a proposal becomes a curation through a review protocol that WP-08 does not implement.

warnings.description: All four, always. Fixed in the schema rather than only in code so a hand-edited file that dropped one is invalid.

legacy_values.description: The project's own former conclusions, copied verbatim from the legacy files. These are exactly the fields that are prohibited inside an evidence record: they are kept here, labelled, rather than deleted.

origins.description: Where each value was read from. A proposal that cannot say which file and row it came from is an assertion with no provenance.

file_sha256.description: So a later reader can tell whether the legacy file has changed since the proposal was written.

ast_path.description: For values recovered from legacy Python by parsing rather than executing it.

linked_evidence.description: Natural keys of evidence records this proposal would be about, matched on an identifier the source itself published. Never matched on a plausible neighbour.

linkage_note.description: Why a proposal is unlinked. An unlinked proposal states that rather than being attached to something nearby.
